units.function: Unit test for a fixed Company invite expiration timestamp exactly 72 hours after creation.
units.dependencyDirection: A pure access-route helper converts caller-supplied creation milliseconds into an absolute Date; no database, policy or identity dependency is exercised.
units.keyDataModels: Invite createdAt milliseconds and expiresAt timestamp.
units.lifecycle: Creation time deterministically produces a three-day expiration time.
units.testAssessment: One deterministic UTC example proves duration arithmetic. It does not test invalid times, exact expiry boundary semantics, clock skew, configurable policy, renewal, revocation, one-time consumption or database enforcement under concurrency.
units.designRationale: Limit the exposure window of a bearer invite while keeping onboarding usable.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs time-bounded, revocable and auditable invitations for real human principals and enterprise identity binding.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the explicit absolute expiry field, but make duration an organization policy and enforce expiry, revocation, intended principal/domain, one-time atomic consumption and identity-provider binding server-side.
units.responsibilityConflict: A timestamp alone does not identify who authorized the invitation, what role/data authority it grants, who consumed it or whether responsibility was reassigned or revoked.
evidence: 73eb2373 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)

units.function: Unit tests for human-readable invite bearer tokens backed by a base64url random suffix.
units.dependencyDirection: The access-route token factory uses runtime randomness and returns a prefixed opaque value; tests inspect only its output format and sample uniqueness.
units.keyDataModels: pcp_invite_ prefix, base64url suffix, estimated entropy and a 1,000-token sample set.
units.lifecycle: A token is generated with a recognizable prefix and random suffix; persistence, delivery, lookup, consumption and deletion are outside this unit.
units.testAssessment: Format, minimum encoded length and sample uniqueness are covered. The test's characters-times-six estimate ignores base64 padding-bit details and does not prove the random source; missing are deterministic source inspection, hashing at rest, constant-time verification, token rotation/revocation, log redaction, one-time atomic use and leak-response tests.
units.designRationale: Provide support-friendly token recognition without sacrificing brute-force resistance.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs safe invitation secrets that can cross email or FDE workflows without becoming durable credentials.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT a distinct prefix and at least 256 random bits, but store only a keyed hash, display once, redact everywhere, scope to organization/role/intended identity, expire and consume atomically, and support revocation and incident evidence.
units.responsibilityConflict: Possession is the only proven authority in this test; the token is not bound to an accountable inviter, recipient identity, approved role or responsibility contract.
evidence: 1cfed0c0 security(invites): widen invite-token entropy and rate-limit public invite endpoints (#8979)

units.function: Unit tests selecting an Agent manager for a join request by searching Company Agents for a root CEO and otherwise the first CEO.
units.dependencyDirection: An unvalidated list of Agent id/role/reportsTo records flows directly into access-route assignment logic; no human principal, organization role registry or authorization policy participates.
units.keyDataModels: Agent id, free-form role, reportsTo and chosen manager Agent ID.
units.lifecycle: No CEO yields no manager; a CEO without reportsTo wins; otherwise array order selects the first CEO.
units.testAssessment: Three small cases document the heuristic. Missing are deterministic ordering, duplicate/root cycles, inactive or compromised Agents, Company isolation, human owners, authorization, delegation, conflicts of interest, escalation and approval/audit behavior.
units.designRationale: Route onboarding work to the nominal top of an Agent organization without requiring a separate human ownership model.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS must route real-person access requests to a qualified accountable human or enterprise IdP policy, never infer legal authority from an Agent title.
units.companyOsFit: Do not reuse this ownership rule. Model accountable human roles and delegated access approvers explicitly; an Agent may prepare evidence or recommendations but cannot be the final identity-admission authority.
units.responsibilityConflict: The heuristic assigns a real-person join workflow to an Agent called CEO, and its fallback depends on input array order. Agent title and reporting topology do not confer legal or security responsibility.
evidence: 73eb2373 docs: use structured agent mentions in paperclip skill (#4103)

units.function: Unit tests for a fixed-window in-memory invitation endpoint limiter keyed by IP address.
units.dependencyDirection: Public-route caller IP and an injected clock feed a process-local service that returns allowed, remaining and retry-after values; no shared store or trusted-proxy layer is involved.
units.keyDataModels: IP key, maxRequests, windowMs, hit timestamps, allowed/remaining and retryAfterSeconds.
units.lifecycle: Requests are counted independently per IP until a fixed window is exhausted; old hits are forgotten after time advances.
units.testAssessment: Tests cover threshold, IP independence and window expiry. Missing are distributed consistency, atomic concurrency, proxy/IP normalization, IPv6/subnet strategy, authenticated principal/device keys, memory bounds and eviction, restart behavior, adaptive abuse controls, observability, lockout recovery and denial-of-service against shared NAT users.
units.designRationale: Add a cheap local barrier against brute-force or enumeration of public invite endpoints.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs layered abuse protection for human onboarding across managed-cloud and self-hosted profiles.
units.companyOsFit: REFERENCE only as a development fallback. Production should use a canonical shared limiter with trusted ingress identity, atomic counters, bounded retention, principal plus network signals, audit telemetry and deployment-profile adapters.
units.responsibilityConflict: Process-local IP state neither proves actor identity nor provides durable evidence; inconsistent replicas can admit excess attempts and shared-IP blocking can deny legitimate employees without an accountable override path.
evidence: 1cfed0c0 security(invites): widen invite-token entropy and rate-limit public invite endpoints (#8979)
